VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A (www.ibge.gov.br contas-nacionais path, plain curl, HTTP 200, 132,905 bytes — this path served genuine bytes where the PNAD Contínua path on the same host returned a WAF 403). IBGE's own page: "As informações da série do Sistema de Contas Nacionais - referência 2010, cabe ressaltar, são apresentadas segundo uma classificação de produtos e atividades integrada com a Classificação Nacional de Atividades Econômicas - CNAE 2.0 e estão em conformidade com o System of national accounts 2008, SNA 2008, manual preparado sob os auspícios da Organização das Nações Unidas - ONU, da Comissão Europeia - Eurostat, do Fundo Monetário Internacional - FMI, da Organização de Cooperação e Desenvolvimento Econômico - OCDE e do Banco Mundial, o que reflete o compromisso do IBGE com a sistemática de revisões periódicas de suas práticas, conforme preconizam as recomendações internacionais." "Em conformidade com" is a methodology claim, not a citation for context, and the sentence names the manual, its edition and its five sponsoring bodies. Brazil's first edge into the international-standards.json layer, and the same shape the corpus already carries for Canadian, German and Antipodean national accounts. Note that sna-2008 is itself superseded by the 2025 SNA per its own node description, with country rollout targeting 2029-2030; IBGE's current rebasing exercise (reference year moving from 2010 to 2021) is the natural moment for that transition, but IBGE's page states only the rebasing, not an SNA edition change, so nothing is asserted about it here.

Destatis states ESA 2010 as the legal basis of the German national accounts in the structured metadata of its own quality report: 'Scope of the statistics: national accounts of the Federation (EVAS No 81) … Legal bases: Regulation (EC) No 549/2013, European System of National and Regional Accounts (ESA) 2010, and supplementary and amending regulations … Periodicity: quarterly, annual'. The same report sets out the mechanism: 'The ESA 2010 is a European Regulation, which is binding for all EU member states as of 1 September 2014 (Council Regulation (EU) No. 549/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 21 May 2013, published in the Official Journal on 26 June 2013). It was implemented in Germany as part of the 2014 general revision. This regulation was amended by Regulation (EU) 2023/734 …'. Two further documents say the same in their own words: the GNI inventory ('in compliance with the European System of National Accounts (ESA) 2010' and 'based on the European System of Accounts (ESA) 2010') and the QNA inventory ('in compliance with the European System of Accounts 2010 (ESA 2010)'). relationship_type is methodology_depends_on rather than uses_data_from: ESA 2010 supplies no figures, it supplies the 'common standards, definitions, classifications and accounting rules that shall be used for compiling accounts and tables' (Regulation 549/2013, Article 1(2)(a)).

Council Regulation (EC) No 479/2009, consolidated text of 01/09/2014, Article 1(1): 'For the purposes of the Protocol on the excessive deficit procedure and of this Regulation, the terms in paragraphs 2 to 6 are defined according to Regulation (EU) No 549/2013 of the European Parliament and the Council of 21 May 2013 on the European system of national and regional accounts in the European Union (hereinafter referred to as ESA 2010). The codes in brackets refer to ESA 2010.' The dependence is operative, not decorative: Article 1(2) defines 'Government' as 'the sector of general government (S.13)... as defined in ESA 2010', Article 1(3) defines 'Government deficit (surplus)' as 'the net borrowing (net lending) (B.9) of the sector of general government (S.13), as defined in ESA 2010', and Article 1(5) defines 'Government debt' by ESA 2010 categories 'currency and deposits (AF.2); debt securities (AF.3) and loans (AF.4)'. 'Are defined according to' is derivation language and is not on Research.1.md section 5a's watchlist. Direction: the EDP Regulation is the dependent, ESA 2010 the depended-on. Quoted with EUR-Lex's in-line amendment markers stripped — the unstripped Article 1(1) reads with the whole clause inside a M2 insertion marker, because the original 2009 text referred to ESA 95.
